parsedVerdict.reasoning: The unit has only one file, src/article/article.service.ts, and its concern holds together: article CRUD, comments, favorites and feed all belong to the article domain. It fails on the other two rubric criteria. First, it bypasses its own data-access abstraction. The constructor injects `articleRepository: Repository<ArticleEntity>`, and most methods use it. But `findAll` and `findFeed` call the global `getRepository(ArticleEntity).createQueryBuilder('article')` instead of the injected repository. That gives the class two inconsistent ways to reach the same data. Second, it duplicates the list query and pagination rule. `findAll` and `findFeed` each repeat the same steps: `qb.orderBy('article.created', 'DESC')`, `getCount()`, the `'limit' in query` and `'offset' in query` checks, and `getMany()`, then build `{articles, articlesCount}`. This rule should live in one shared helper. There is also smaller repeated logic: `favorite` and `unFavorite` each keep `favoriteCount` in step with `user.favorites` in their own code, and the find-by-slug lookup is repeated in every method.
